rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked each phase's forcing function against the registry-prompt text (curriculum/prompts/threat-model-with-stride-{1,2,3}.md), not just the body lead-in. Phase 1: prompt-1 itself instructs 'invoke the stride skill on the access-surface map... Run stride in a subagent... Don't pick yet — I'll decide next.' Phase 2: prompt-2 enacts 'name the worst case first' in the fence — 'Start by proposing the most plausible incident story... then map that story to the STRIDE class it best fits... I'll steer if the story or mapping misses' — the incident-story-before-classification sequencing is IN the fence; body lines 30-31 only narrate the discipline without re-scripting it. Phase 3: prompt-3 requires 'Alternatives considered names the 2-3 options we didn't pick and one line on why' — the mechanic the leap test's second falsifiable outcome depends on is in the fence. Body line 32 ('One threat, not five') and line 27 ('reject most... that rejection is the point') are framing, not the count-script the rule's removal test would flag — cutting them loses framing, not pedagogy, since the operative pick-one forcing function already lives in the -2 fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full body re-read above the maintainer fence (lines 1-84): no 'discuss with', 'share with your neighbor', 'take N seconds and compare', or any authored pause/comparison cue. Every sentence is about the work — the STRIDE walk, the pick, the ADR, the worktree check, the auto-load reveal. 'Check where the ADR landed' (lines 60-64) reads as agent-behavior diagnosis, not a room-management cue. Push-back moves and Watch-fors live entirely below the maintainer fence (line 85+), addressed to the trainer, never scripted into student-facing text.
